chapters.summary: Hosea 1 records how the prophet, at God's command, marries a promiscuous woman as a sign of Israel's unfaithfulness, and foretells both God's coming judgment and Israel's future restoration.
keyPoints: God commands Hosea to marry Gomer, a promiscuous woman, as a sign of Israel's unfaithfulness to him.
He names his three children, foretelling judgment on the house of Jehu and mercy toward Israel.
It is prophesied that Judah and Israel will one day be reunited under a single leader.
chapters.application: When we drift away from God in our own lives, let us remember that his love never lets go - he calls us to turn back and promises restoration and blessing.

chapters.summary: This chapter uses the metaphor of marriage to describe Israel's relationship with God, declaring that Israel will be punished for worshiping idols, yet in the end God will win her back and rebuild that relationship.
keyPoints: God accuses Israel of adultery, forsaking him to chase after Baal, and declares that she will be punished.
God will hedge up her way so that she cannot find her lovers, driving her to turn back to him.
God promises that after the punishment, he will lead Israel into the wilderness, make a new covenant with her, and make her his people once again.
chapters.application: We too sometimes drift from God, but he disciplines us in love so that we will turn back. When we find ourselves in hardship, let us examine our hearts and turn to him - he will surely receive us again.

chapters.summary: Hosea obeys God's command to buy back his unfaithful wife, a sign of God's love for backsliding Israel and his promise of restoration.
keyPoints: God commands Hosea to love the adulterous woman once more, showing that God's love for Israel never lets go.
Hosea buys his wife back with silver and barley, foreshadowing the price God would pay to redeem his people.
Israel will go many days without king or sacrifice, but will afterward return and seek God, and receive his grace.
chapters.application: However weak we are or however far we have wandered from God, his love for us never changes. May we turn back to him and know his forgiveness and restoration.

chapters.summary: God brings a charge against the people of Israel: there is no truth, no kindness, no knowledge of God among them, for they have rejected knowledge, the priests have failed in their duty, and the people follow idols - so judgment must come.
keyPoints: God brings a charge against the inhabitants of the land, for there is no truth, no kindness, and no knowledge of God among them.
The priests have rejected knowledge and forgotten God's law, so the people perish for lack of it.
Israel commits spiritual adultery through idol worship, forsaking God like a harlot, and so must be punished.
chapters.application: Today, may we long to know God, hold fast to his word, turn away from idols, and worship him in spirit and truth, lest we perish for lack of knowledge.

chapters.summary: Through Hosea, God declares judgment on Israel and Judah for breaking covenant and for their pride; though they seek God, they cannot find him, until at last they acknowledge their guilt and seek him.
keyPoints: Priests, royal house, and people alike are judged for their sin, as God punishes their pride and their whoredom.
Israel and Judah seek God in their distress, but he hides his face from them for a time, because their repentance is not sincere.
God declares that he will return to his place until they acknowledge their guilt and earnestly seek him in their affliction.
chapters.application: When we drift from God, let us examine our own hearts and repent sincerely - not seeking him only in hardship, but holding fast to our faith in everyday life.

chapters.summary: This chapter calls the people to return to God, declaring that he delights in steadfast love more than sacrifice, and pointing out how fleeting their devotion is, like the morning mist.
keyPoints: God, having torn them, will heal them, and having wounded them, will bind them up - showing forth his steadfast love.
The people's devotion is like the morning mist, gone as quickly as it comes, lacking any lasting faithfulness.
God delights in steadfast love and the knowledge of himself more than in burnt offerings and religious ritual.
chapters.application: Let us examine whether our faith is lasting or merely a passing form. May we respond to God's mercy with sincere, enduring love rather than fleeting zeal.

chapters.summary: This chapter exposes the depth of Israel's sin and the corruption of her leaders; though they cry out to God, they do so without sincerity, and judgment will come at last for their rebellion.
keyPoints: Even as God would heal Israel, her iniquity is exposed - her leaders do evil, and no one calls upon God.
The king and the princes, like a heated oven, indulge in drunkenness and plot betrayal.
Israel, like a cake not turned, relies on foreign nations, not knowing that God has already taken note of her evil.
chapters.application: Let us examine our own hearts, and not deceive God with false piety; let us repent sincerely and turn from sin, for God sees all things and will surely guide us onto the right path.

chapters.summary: God rebukes Israel for breaking covenant and worshiping idols, and warns that judgment will come, for they have sown the wind and shall reap the whirlwind.
keyPoints: Israel breaks God's law, sets up kings of their own choosing, and makes idols, provoking God's anger.
Though they offer sacrifices, they do so insincerely, and God will remember their guilt and punish their transgressions.
Israel turns to foreign nations, stubborn as a wild donkey, and will be carried off to Assyria for forsaking God.
chapters.application: Let us examine whether we have strayed from the true path in our faith; rather than relying on worldly power or empty religious form, let us depend wholeheartedly on God and worship him in sincerity.

chapters.summary: Hosea declares that Israel will be punished for idolatry and spiritual adultery, carried off to a foreign land, and stripped of her festivals and her home.
keyPoints: Israel will be punished for worshiping Baal and playing the harlot on every threshing floor, and her joy will turn to sorrow.
Ephraim's glory will fly away like a bird - she will bear no children, for she has forsaken God and been given over to the sword.
The prophet warns the people that because their guilt runs deep, God will call it to account, and they will wander in exile in Egypt and Assyria.
chapters.application: Let us turn away from idols and trust in God alone, lest we lose his presence and his blessing.

chapters.summary: Israel comes under God's judgment for idolatry and broken covenant, yet God still calls them to seek righteousness, promising mercy to those who repent.
keyPoints: Israel is like a luxuriant vine, but the more her fruit increases, the more she multiplies her sin, and so brings ruin on herself.
They rely on idols and false alliances, which will only lead to their destruction.
God calls them to sow righteousness, reap steadfast love, and seek him.
chapters.application: Let us examine our hearts for any hidden idols, and turn back to God, treating others with righteousness and love - he will surely watch over us and guide us.

chapters.summary: With a father's love, God calls out to Israel; though they are rebellious, he still has compassion on them and will not destroy them.
keyPoints: God recalls how he loved Israel from her childhood, calling her out of Egypt.
Israel only strayed further from God, offering sacrifices to Baal, yet God still taught them to walk.
God, moved by compassion, holds back his anger and does not carry out destruction in the heat of his wrath, for he is God and not man.
chapters.application: Even when we stumble again and again, God's love never gives up on us. May we respond with gratitude, no longer wandering away, but returning to his embrace.

chapters.summary: Hosea 12 rebukes Israel's deceit and ingratitude and calls them to return to God, using Jacob's story to remind them of God's faithfulness and steadfast love.
keyPoints: Israel deals falsely with others and quarrels with Judah, yet considers herself rich and does not turn to God.
God reminds his chosen people of their forefather Jacob's humility and effort, and of how God watched over and delivered him.
The prophet calls the people to repent, to keep justice and steadfast love, and to wait on God, for he will surely punish their sin.
chapters.application: Let us ask ourselves whether, caught up in our busy lives, we have forgotten God. May we follow Jacob's example of humility, treat others with honesty and love, and wait on God, for he will surely guide us.

chapters.summary: Through Hosea, God declares that Israel will perish because of idolatry and pride, yet promises that in the last days he will save them.
keyPoints: Ephraim was once honored, but sinned through worshiping Baal, and now vanishes like the morning mist and the early dew.
The people forget God's provision and grow proud in heart, and so will be devoured like prey by wild beasts and struck by the sword.
Though God attacks like a lion, he still holds on to mercy, promising to redeem them from the grave and from death.
chapters.application: Let us always remember God's grace, and never grow proud because of prosperity. Even when we fall, God still longs to save us - let us repent and turn back to him.

chapters.summary: In the final chapter of Hosea, the prophet calls Israel to return to God, who promises to heal their backsliding, love them freely, and make them blossom like the lily and take root like the trees of Lebanon, bearing fruit that belongs to him.
keyPoints: The prophet calls the people to return to the LORD, to confess their guilt, and to come with words of repentance, asking for forgiveness.
God promises to heal their backsliding and love them freely, making Israel blossom like the lily and take root like the trees of Lebanon.
Ephraim will no longer worship idols; God will care for them and make them fruitful, and whoever is wise will understand his ways.
chapters.application: However far we have wandered from God, if we turn back to him, he will heal and forgive us, causing us to take root and grow anew, and bear the fruit of life.
